title: The Café Revenue Mystery
summary: Mama Bisi's café is packed every day, yet her printout says revenue fell 40%. Find what she really earned.

client.name: Mama Bisi
brief: Every table is full, yet my weekly printout says revenue crashed by 40%!
The laptop on the patio has the POS ledger. Check what we really earned each day.
client.thanks: You've saved me a sleepless week. Here's your fee, my dear.

starterSql:
-- BGAP Analytics Workstation — Chapter 01: The Café Revenue Mystery
-- Mama Bisi wants to know what the café really earned each day.
-- Start by looking at the raw ledger, then build your answer.

SELECT *
FROM sales
LIMIT 20;

columns.name: sale_at
columns.desc: Date and time the order was placed

hints.title: Hint 1: Not every row is money
hints.desc: Some rows are voided tickets (mistakes cancelled straight away) or refunds. They never became revenue.

hints.title: Hint 2: Keep only completed sales
hints.desc: Filter the rows to completed transactions before adding anything up.

hints.title: Hint 3: Shape of the answer
hints.desc: One row per day: turn sale_at into a date, and add up quantity × unit_price for each day.

findings.claim: Why does the printout show revenue falling while the café is full?

options.text: Customer numbers fell sharply in the afternoons.
Customers are as many as ever; voided duplicate tickets and refunds were distorting the gross figures.
Heavy catering discounts wiped out the margins.

findings.claim: Which day earned the most recognised revenue?

successFeedback: Footfall is fine. Voided duplicates and refunds were inflating the gross figure; completed sales show the café is doing well (₦115,500, ₦126,000 and ₦91,350 a day).

fixtures.purpose: The ledger you can see in the terminal
fixtures.failHint: Your daily totals don’t match Mama Bisi’s ledger.
Some orders that never earned money are still in your totals. Check payment_status.

fixtures.purpose: Orders with several items and non-round prices
fixtures.failHint: Revenue should account for how many of each item were sold.
Sales near midnight are landing on the wrong day.

fixtures.purpose: A day with no completed sales
fixtures.failHint: Refunded or voided sales are adding revenue to a day that had none.

evidence.title: Mama Bisi's receipt book
evidence.text: Mama Bisi's handwritten book of the week's tickets. Beside TX-1006 (1 Oct, 'Accidental Duplicate Order', 5 × ₦6,000): "VOID: rang it twice." TX-1005 (1 Oct, avocado toast & tea): "Refunded, tea was cold." TX-1010 (2 Oct): "VOID." TX-1014 (3 Oct, catering test order, ₦50,000): "Refunded by transfer." The printout adds every one of these to the takings.
